clue.text: Colour put on metal base by wayward child reveals artist

indicators.note: the next pieces are placed after the colour in the charade
the child piece is set beside the others at the end

parts.note: to colour is to tint
OR is gold, a metal in heraldry
E is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

indicators.note: a wayward thing goes astray, so the letters of the child word are jumbled

parts.note: a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: An artist's naughty youngster has slopped paint over a metal stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' reads as a stand or pedestal, but here it is the mathematician's base of natural logarithms; 'wayward' jumbles the small child into the last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintoretto was a Venetian painter of the sixteenth century, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Her daughter learned the king's English in play

definitions.text: Her daughter learned the king's English in play

parts.words: Her daughter learned the king's English in play
parts.note: in Shakespeare's Henry V the French princess Katherine takes an English lesson; the clue asks for her mother, the French queen

explanation.definitionFit: Queen Isabel of France is the mother of Princess Katherine, who learns English words in Act 3 of Henry V.

clue.text: Waugh character gets theatre award at the end

parts.note: the Tony is the American award for Broadway theatre
last means at the end

explanation.surface: A character from Evelyn Waugh finally wins a prize for the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Last is the hero of Evelyn Waugh's novel A Handful of Dust.

clue.text: Exposure, perhaps like one of William le Queux's, concerning spooks

definitions.text: perhaps like one of William le Queux's, concerning spooks

explanation.definitionFit: A disclosure is an exposure, and William le Queux wrote Revelations of the Secret Service, about spies.

clue.text: Grand Hotel starts by concealing satellite

indicators.note: the words Grand Hotel starts conceal the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A grand hotel begins to hide a space satellite.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from 'hoTEL STARts'; 'Grand' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Telstar was the first communications satellite to relay television across the Atlantic, in 1962.

clue.text: Fairy-tale monster spills gore

indicators.note: something spilled is scattered about, so the letters of gore are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monster from a fairy tale sheds blood.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant found in fairy stories.

clue.text: She was one of Jennifer Johnston's novel outsiders in 1977

definitions.text: She was one of Jennifer Johnston's novel outsiders in 1977

parts.words: She was one of Jennifer Johnston's novel outsiders in 1977
parts.note: Johnston's 1977 novel Shadows on Our Skin pairs a Derry boy with a young teacher, both outsiders; the clue asks for the teacher's first name

explanation.definitionFit: Kathleen Doherty is the young schoolteacher who befriends Joe Logan in Jennifer Johnston's Shadows on Our Skin.

clue.text: Quarrel comes down on illustrator

parts.note: a row is a quarrel
to land on something is to come down on it

explanation.surface: An argument descends on an artist who draws pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Rowlandson was a Georgian caricaturist famous for his satirical drawings.

clue.text: Lorca's romantic Romany

parts.note: Federico García Lorca's ballad collection Romancero ... takes its name from the Spanish word for a Gypsy

explanation.definitionFit: Gitano is Spanish for a Gypsy or Romany man, the word in the title of Lorca's Romancero gitano.

clue.text: Fair creation of Compton MacKenzie

explanation.definitionFit: A carnival is a funfair or festival, and Carnival is a 1912 novel by Compton Mackenzie.

clue.text: The land's laid waste for Henri Beyle

indicators.note: ground laid waste is wrecked, so the letters of the words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: The country is ravaged on behalf of a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's gives its S here, as part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Beyle was the real name of the French novelist who wrote under his famous pen name.

clue.text: Jeremy Bentham's was for the constitution

definitions.text: Jeremy Bentham's was for the constitution

parts.words: Jeremy Bentham's was for the constitution
parts.note: the philosopher Jeremy Bentham wrote a pamphlet whose title begins with an appeal on behalf of the constitution

explanation.definitionFit: Bentham published A Plea for the Constitution in 1803, an earnest appeal or request.

clue.text: Exile's trap to be dismantled for sculptor

indicators.note: something dismantled is taken apart, so the letters of the two words are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A snare set for a banished man is taken apart for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Praxiteles was a celebrated Greek sculptor of the fourth century BC.

clue.text: Hardy, but lukewarm

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy wrote the novel A Laodicean, and a Laodicean is someone half-hearted, like the tepid church in Revelation.

clue.text: English county manservant (with bulldog)

explanation.definitionFit: Derbyshire is a Midlands county of England, and also the name of a valet in a story featuring a bulldog.

clue.text: "is Switzerland, speaking pure German and with history added" (J. E. Morpurgo)

definitions.text: "is Switzerland, speaking pure German and with history added" (J. E. Morpurgo)

parts.words: "is Switzerland, speaking pure German and with history added" (J. E. Morpurgo)
parts.note: the clue is a quotation from J. E. Morpurgo with its opening word missing: a German-speaking country with a long imperial past

explanation.definitionFit: The Alpine republic speaks German, borders Switzerland and carries the Habsburg imperial past.

clue.text: Elvira's sort of gaff user recorded by V. S. Naipaul

definitions.text: Elvira's sort of gaff user recorded by V. S. Naipaul

parts.words: Elvira's sort of gaff user recorded by V. S. Naipaul
parts.note: Naipaul's comic novel about an election in a Trinidad county takes its title from the right to vote of Elvira's people

explanation.definitionFit: Naipaul's novel The Suffrage of Elvira is about an election, suffrage being the right to vote.

clue.text: Simon Raven had them in low places

definitions.text: Simon Raven had them in low places

parts.words: Simon Raven had them in low places
parts.note: Simon Raven's first Alms for Oblivion novel is titled after companions found in humble places

explanation.definitionFit: Simon Raven's 1965 novel is Friends in Low Places, friends being companions.

clue.text: College friend of Lucy Snowe

explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel is a Cambridge college, and Paul Emanuel is the professor who befriends Lucy Snowe in Charlotte Brontë's Villette.

clue.text: "My heart to every Vice inclin'd, / The Sinner's— Sin bewrays" (John Wesley)

definitions.text: "My heart to every Vice inclin'd, / The Sinner's— Sin bewrays" (John Wesley)

parts.words: "My heart to every Vice inclin'd, / The Sinner's— Sin bewrays" (John Wesley)
parts.note: a quotation from a Wesley hymn with one word missing, meaning nearest or most intimate

explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Wesley's line means most intimate, the sin held nearest the heart.

clue.text: How difficult may it be to translate Dante's vision of hell?

definitions.text: How difficult may it be to translate Dante's vision of hell?

parts.words: How difficult may it be to translate Dante's vision of hell?
parts.note: the reply is an adverb meaning fiendishly, punning on the Inferno, the first part of Dante's Divine Comedy

explanation.definitionFit: Hellishly, fiendishly difficult, with a pun on Dante's Inferno.

clue.text: Signify Miss Duffy's time

explanation.definitionFit: To signify is to intend or denote, and Carol Ann Duffy's poetry collection is titled Mean Time.

clue.text: Well-connected investigator seen in Passage to the North

parts.note: an alley is a narrow passage
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A detective with friends in high places is spotted in a book about heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: Roderick Alleyn, Ngaio Marsh's detective, is well connected: his brother is a baronet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ngaio Marsh's Scotland Yard detective comes from an aristocratic family.

clue.text: Arrange singer an income

indicators.note: to arrange music is to rework it, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Organise a vocalist and a salary.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are the money a person is paid, their income.

clue.text: Outstanding feature of Untouchables leader

explanation.definitionFit: A ness is a headland that juts out, and Eliot Ness led the Prohibition agents called the Untouchables.

clue.text: Heroic new ruse for students from Garden School

parts.note: epic poetry is heroic

indicators.note: a new version of the word ruse rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: A grand fresh ploy for pupils of a gardening college.
explanation.walkthrough: Epicurus taught in his Garden at Athens, so his followers are students of the Garden School.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Epicurus, whose school met in his garden, were called by his name.

clue.text: German cherub followed by second socialist

indicators.note: the abbreviation comes after the German word

parts.note: Engel is the German word for an angel

explanation.surface: A German angel comes after a second socialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels co-wrote The Communist Manifesto with Marx, a founder of socialist thought.

clue.text: Scottish county artist

explanation.definitionFit: Sutherland is a former county in the far north of Scotland, and Graham Sutherland was an English painter.
